rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.l1: The e7-pawn advances to e5 and drives the d4-knight away. With that, the d7-pawn has no neighbour behind it: the c-pawn was traded, and the e-pawn has gone ahead.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.l2: The knight goes to b5 and threatens to come to d6 with check.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.l3: Black covers d6 with the pawn. Now it is backward: the e5-pawn has gone ahead, and the e4-pawn watches d5. The d-file, with no white pawn, is half-open for White.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.l4: The c3-knight goes to d5, the square in front of the backward pawn. It is a weak square: no black pawn can attack it, and only the black pieces can contest it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.l5: Why does Black accept it? Black gained space and time by driving the knight away. In positions like this, a backward pawn is only created with something in return: the position decides.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.e1: Attack: a backward pawn has fallen behind its neighbouring pawns and cannot advance safely. No pawn can defend it: only the pieces protect it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.sveshnikov.e2: This is the Sicilian Defence, on the way to the Sveshnikov Variation. Black has already traded the c-pawn, and the d7-pawn is still on its starting square.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.p: Find the move that captures the backward pawn.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.certo: The rook captures the e3-pawn with check. If the white queen recaptures, the g1-queen takes it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.revela: The rook captures the e3-pawn with check: two attackers against one defender, and if the white queen recaptures, the g1-queen takes it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.err.g1a1.1: The queen gives check on a1, but leaves the diagonal that attacked the e3-pawn.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.err.g1a1.2: The king goes to d3 and gets out of check. Now the king and the queen defend the e3-pawn, and only the rook attacks it: it holds.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.err.g1a1.3: Back to the position: count the attackers and defenders of the e3-pawn and capture it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.err.g1e3.1: The queen captures the e3-pawn with check, but the f3-queen defends it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.err.g1e3.2: The white queen captures the queen. After the rook recaptures, the queens are off the board, and White is better.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.err.g1e3.3: Back to the position: capture the e3-pawn with the piece that keeps the g1-queen in reserve.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.fora: That move does not capture the e3-pawn. Use one of the black pieces that already attack it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.volta: Try again: capture the backward pawn.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.e1: Attack: now let's think from Black's side. This position comes from a game played on Lichess. White's e3-pawn is backward: the d4- and f5-pawns have gone ahead.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.e2: The e-file has no black pawn: it is half-open for Black. The e8-rook and the g1-queen attack the e3-pawn, and only the f3-queen defends it.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.l0: On e3, the rook gives check and is defended by the g1-queen.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.l1: If the king stepped out of check, or the rook or bishop blocked it on d3, the rook would capture the f3-queen. So the white queen captures the rook.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.l2: The black queen recaptures with check. Black gave the rook but won the pawn and the queen.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.contra.l3: On a half-open file, the backward pawn is a fixed target: no pawn can come to defend it. Count attackers and defenders; if they are equal, bring one more piece to the file before capturing.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.p: Find the move that uses the backward pawn to clear the way for the rook.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.certo: The pawn advances to c4 with check and leaves the third rank: the e3-rook now attacks the one on a3.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.revela: The pawn advances to c4 with check: the rank between the rooks opens, and the e3-rook now attacks the one on a3.
The rook gives check on d3, but leaves the third rank, and the c3-pawn is still in the way.
The king goes to c4 and attacks the d3-rook and the c3-pawn.
Back to the position: look for a move of the c3-pawn.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.fora: That move does not use the c3-pawn. Look for a move by it or by the e3-rook.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.e1: Attack: White again, now with the backward pawn on your side. This position comes from a game played on Lichess. Your c3-pawn is backward: the b4-pawn has gone ahead.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.e2: The e3-rook and the black rook on a3 are on the same rank, but the c3-pawn stands between them.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.l0: The c4-pawn gives check, and the rank between the e3-rook and the a3-rook is clear.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.l1: The black king must get out of check, and captures the pawn. Capturing with the b5-pawn would not save the a3-rook either.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.l2: The rook captures the one on a3. White gave the backward pawn and won a rook.
rot.backwardPawn.ideia.proprio.l3: Your backward pawn is a fixed weakness. In positions like this, get rid of it when the advance wins something: here it opened the rook's rank.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra.l.3: The knight goes to c5 and attacks the e6-queen and the a6-rook at the same time.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra.l.4: The queen escapes to c8, from where it defends the rook along the diagonal.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra.l.5: The knight captures the rook. If the queen recaptures, White has won the rook for the knight.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra.l.6: In positions like this, the square in front of the backward pawn is a great post for the knight: no pawn can drive it away from c5. Here, from c5, it attacked two pieces.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: White again, in another Lichess game. Black's c6-pawn is backward: the d5-pawn has gone ahead, and there is no black pawn on the b-file.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra.2: The c5-square, in front of it, is weak: no black pawn can attack it, and the d4-pawn defends it.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra2.l.3: The rook captures the backward pawn with check.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra2.l.4: The king recaptures the rook. If it went to d3 or e3, the c4-rook would capture the one on e4.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra2.l.5: The black king captures the e4-rook, which was left undefended.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra2.l.6: By capturing, the white king moved away from the e4-rook, and it fell. Along the half-open file, the black rook gave itself for the backward pawn and won the other rook: the pawn endgame is Black's.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: now let's think from Black's side, in another Lichess game. White's c4-pawn is backward: the d5-pawn has gone ahead, and there is no white pawn on the b-file.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.regra2.2: The c-file has no black pawn, and the c7-rook attacks the c4-pawn along it. The white king defends the pawn and also the e4-rook.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.excecao.l.3: The backward pawn advances to b3 anyway and attacks the c2-pawn.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.excecao.l.4: The c2-pawn captures on b3. If it did not, the b3-pawn would capture it or advance to the last rank.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.excecao.l.5: Now the c3-pawn's path is clear: it advances to c2, and no white piece reaches c1 in time.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.excecao.l.6: The backward pawn is not only a weakness: here its advance cleared the way for its neighbour to queen. Before judging it, see what it can do: the position decides.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: Black again, now with the backward pawn on your side, on b4: the c3-pawn has gone ahead, and there is no black pawn on the a-file.
rot.backwardPawn.demos.excecao.2: The white c2-pawn watches b3, the square in front of the b4-pawn, and blocks the c3-pawn.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.casa.enunciado: Black's d6-pawn is backward. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.casa.fim: The queen went to d5, the weak square in front of the backward pawn, with check, and attacked the c6-knight. The king got out of check, and the queen captured the knight.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.casa.err.g4e6: 24.Be6+? gives check, but after 24...Kh8 the bishop attacks nothing else, and the position is equal.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.posto.enunciado: White's e3-pawn is backward. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.posto.fim: The knight went to e4, the weak square in front of the backward pawn, defended by the d5-pawn, and attacked the d6-rook and the d2-bishop. The rook escaped, and the knight captured the bishop.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.posto.err.g5f3: 46...Nf3? attacks the d2-bishop, but 47.Bc1 saves it, and the position is equal.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.posto.err.e7e4: 46...Re4? attacks nothing undefended, and 47.Rxd5 captures the d5-pawn: White is better.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.proprio.enuncia: Your d4-pawn is backward. Is it only a weakness here, or can it help? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.proprio.fim: The backward pawn advanced with check and left the fourth rank: the a4-rook now attacked the one on f4. The king captured the pawn, and the rook captured the rook.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.proprio.err.a4a: 48.Ra6+? gives check, but after 48...Kb7 the rook wins nothing, and Black, two pawns up, is better.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.proprio.err.d3c: 48.Kc4? defends the d4-pawn, but 48...Rf1 activates the rook, and Black, two pawns up, is better.
rot.backwardPawn.pratica.proprio.err.d3e: 48.Ke3? attacks the f4-rook, but 48...g5 defends it, and Black, two pawns up, is better.
